books.title: Non-Violent Communication. A Language of Life
books.author: Marshall B. Rosenberg
books.note: A communication and conflict-resolution process focusing on how to express ourselves in a way that inspires empathy in others, and how to listen to them empathically in turn.

books.title: Tribe
books.author: Sebastian Junger
books.note: Explores what can be learned from tribal societies about loyalty, belonging, and meaning.  How for many veterans war feels better than peace, and adversity can turn out to be a blessing and disasters are better remembered than vacations.

books.title: The Yosemite
books.author: John Muir
books.note: He wrote about his experience in the outdoors and how it changed his life especially in the Sierras. He founded the Sierra Club.  Really powerful and inspiring reading for those who are lost and could benefit being in the wilderness.

books.title: My First Summer in the Sierra
books.author: John Muir

books.title: Leadership and Self Deception
books.author: Arbinger Institute
books.note: This book explores how we all view and treat others as objects to help us accomplish our goals (termed being "in the box") as opposed to viewing others as people, with their own hopes and dreams (being "out of the box").

books.title: Man's Search for meaning
books.author: Viktor Frankl
books.note: Viktor Frankl is writing about his experience as a Jew in the Holocaust. He explains how he was able to be happy in the worst of circumstances. It involved identifying a purpose in life to feel positively about, and then immersive imagining that outcome.

books.title: A long Way Gone
books.author: Ishmael Beah
books.note: Memoirs written by Ishmael Beah, an author from Sierra Leone.  His firsthand account of his time as a child soldier during the civil war in Sierra Leone.

books.title: Wild at Heart
books.author: John Eldredge
books.note: It’s on the subject of men recovering their masculine heart as defined in the image of a passionate God

books.title: Crazy Love
books.author: Francis Chan
books.note: Deals with the idea of the average Christian’s love of God and learning how to further develop those feelings into a “crazy, relentless, all-powerful love

books.title: The Things They Carried
books.author: Tim O'Brien
books.note: A classic work of American literature that has not stopped changing minds and lives since it burst onto the literary scene, The Things They Carried is a ground-breaking meditation on war, memory, imagination, and the redemptive power of storytelling.

books.title: The Alchemist
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.note: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure. Santiago's journey teaches us about the essential wisdom of listening to our hearts, of recognizing opportunity and learning to read the omens strewn along life's path, and, most importantly, to follow our dreams.

books.title: The Book of Five Rings
books.author: Miyamoto Musashi
books.note:
Zen philosophy offers tactics and strategies as relevant to personal success today as they were to 17th-century samurai. The Five Rings speaks to every age about the essential roles of harmony and self-mastery in our lives. Engaging teaching to those who
seek a model for personal development in a straight-forward and unpretentious way.

books.title: How Not to Die
books.author: Dr. Michael Greger and Gene Stone
books.note: Discovering the foods scientifically proven to prevent and reverse disease will help you reach your optimal state of wellness and even reverse your current condition.

books.title: The Four Agreements
books.author: Miguel Ruiz
books.note: Reveals the source of self-limiting beliefs that rob us of joy and create needless suffering. Based on ancient Toltec wisdom, that can rapidly transform our lives to a new experience of freedom, true happiness, and love.

books.title: Learned Optimism
books.author: Martin E.P. Seligman
books.note: Demonstrates how optimism enhances the quality of life, and how anyone can learn to practice it. How to break a habit, develop a more constructive explanatory style for interpreting your behavior, and experience the benefits of a more positive interior dialogue. These skills can help break up depression, boost your immune system, better develop your potential.

books.title: Women Who Run With the Wolves
books.author: Clarissa Pinkola Estés
books.note: Analyses myths, fairy tales, folk tales and stories from different cultures to uncover the Wild Woman archetype of the feminine psyche. The notion of the archetype is associated with the work of Carl Jung.

books.title: Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking
books.author: Malcolm Gladwell
books.note: Blink reveals that great decision makers aren't those who process the most information or spend the most time deliberating, but those who have perfected the art of "thin-slicing"-filtering the very few factors that matter from an overwhelming number of variables.

books.title: The Gifts of Imperfection
books.author: Brené Brown
books.note: Brené Brown, a leading expert on shame, authenticity, and belonging, shares ten guideposts on the power of Wholehearted living—a way of engaging with the world from a place of worthiness.

books.title: Codependent No More
books.author: Melody Beattie
books.note: A simple, straightforward, readable map of the perplexing world of codependency--charting the path to freedom and a lifetime of healing, hope, and happiness.

books.title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
books.author: Garth Stein
books.note: A heart-wrenching but deeply funny and ultimately uplifting story of family, love, loyalty, and hope--a captivating look at the wonders and absurdities of human life . . . as only a dog could tell it.

books.title: You are a Badass
books.author: Jen Sincero
books.note: Identify and change the self-sabotaging beliefs and behaviors that stop you from getting what you want, Create a life you totally love.

books.title: Who Moved My Cheese
books.author: Spencer Johnson
books.note: In this artful way, Spencer Johnson introduces the reader to his fable on how to cope positively with change.

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.note: Heartbreaking story of the unlikely friendship between a wealthy boy and the son of his father’s servant, caught in the tragic sweep of history. A powerful story of friendship, it is also about the power of reading, the price of betrayal, and the possibility of redemption; and an exploration of the power of fathers over sons

books.title: Drinking in the Rain
books.author: Alix Kates Shulman
books.note: Memoirs of an Ex-Prom Queen, left a city life dense with political activism,  went to live alone on an island off the coast of Maine. In a cabin with no plumbing, power, or telephone, she found that she was learning to live all over again.

books.title: Woodswoman
books.author: Anne LaBastille
books.note: Through luck and perseverance, she found the ideal spot: a 20-acre parcel of land in the Adirondack mountains, where she built the cozy, primitive log cabin that became her permanent home. She captures the struggle to balance her need for companionship and love with her desire for independence and solitude.

books.title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
books.author: Mark Haddon
books.note: Christopher John Francis Boone knows all the countries of the world and their capitals and every prime number up to 7,057. He relates well to animals but has no understanding of human emotions. He cannot stand to be touched. And he detests the color yellow.

books.title: The Brain That Changes Itself
books.author: Norman Doidge
books.note: An astonishing new science called "neuroplasticity" is overthrowing the centuries-old notion that the human brain is immutable.  From stroke patients learning to speak again to the remarkable case of a woman born with half a brain that rewired itself to work as a whole.
books.fix: Spreadsheet listed the wrong author and title.

books.title: The Nature Fix
books.author: Florence Williams
books.note: Williams investigates cutting-edge research as she travels to fragrant cypress forests in Korea to meet the rangers who administer “forest healing programs,” to the green hills of Scotland and its “Eco therapeutic” approach to caring for the mentally ill.  Therapeutic recreation accounts from ID and WV illustrating how time in nature is not a luxury but is in fact essential to our humanity.

books.title: The Last Child in the Woods
books.author: Richard Louv
books.note: Lauv brings together cutting-edge research showing that direct exposure to nature is essential for healthy childhood development-physical, emotional, and spiritual. What's more, nature is a potent therapy for depression, obesity, and ADD. Environment-based education dramatically improves standardized test scores and grade point averages and develops skills in problem solving, critical thinking, and decision making.

books.title: Switch: How to change things when things are hard
books.author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
books.note: Why do we insist on seeing the obstacles rather than the goal? Chip and Dan Heath tackle this in their compelling and insightful new book. They argue that we need only understand how our minds function in order to unlock shortcuts to switches in behavior. Illustrating their ideas with scientific studies and remarkable real-life turnarounds

books.title: Thinking Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.note: Explains the two systems that drive the way we think. System 1 is the fast, intuitive, and emotional; and system 2 is the slower, more deliberative and more logical. Understanding the two systems and integrating them into our lives can have a profound effect of cognitive basis in various ways.

books.title: The Art of Choosing
books.author: Sheena Iyengar
books.note: Sheena Iyengar asks the difficult questions about how and why people make choices- Is the desire for choice innate or bound by culture? Why do people sometimes choose against our best interests? How much control do people really have over what they choose?

books.title: Stumbling on Happiness
books.author: Daniel Gilbert
books.note: Scientific discoveries about the uniquely human ability to imagine the future, and about our capacity to predict how much we will like it when we get there.
